chunks: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari from his uncle Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'rin from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ya'qub al-Ahmar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the month of Ramadan always complete (30 days)?' He said: 'No, rather it is a month among the months (implying it can be 29 or 30 days).'

key_terms.شَهْرٌ مِنَ الشُّهُورِ: A month among the months (implying variability)

ai.seo_question: Is the month of Ramadan always 30 days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the assumption that Ramadan is perpetually thirty days, affirming its status as a lunar month subject to the Islamic practice of *ru'yah* (observation). This clarification underscores the flexibility of the calendar and the authority of local sighting in determining the month's duration, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the start and end of fasting.
